title: USB: fix usbip dissector for fragmented non-iso packets
description:
number_of_packets (0x18) is 0xffffffff for non-iso transfers
so don't add -1 * 4 * 4 = 16 bytes to the expected packet length

Signed-off-by: Steve Bennett <steveb@workware.net.au>

notes.body:
I've tested this build and can confirm the USBIP packets are now correctly dissected.
Prior to this fix the packets would be incorrectly defined as such:
![image](/uploads/26076c0e6311305d43bc7d568c67bb1a/image.png)

The packets are now correctly defined like so:
![image](/uploads/dea1881eb6d816b5f3b1236c9387e294/image.png)

Both of those screenshots are from frames 4-21 of the same capture.

BTW, I see why my indent was wrong. The file has these modelines:

` * ex: set shiftwidth=2 tabstop=8 expandtab:`

Seems like this should be shiftwidth=4

It seems that the transfer type cannot be determined from USBIP header itself, or am I missing something? In other words, is it up to the usbip server to keep track of endpoint types based on configuration descriptor and then assign correct transfer type based on the endpoint type?

If above is true, then it seems fine to just depend on 0xffffffff being negative.
Yes, that's correct. Without seeing the endpoint descriptors it's not possible to know
But still better to test explicitly for 0xffffffff. I will make that change
Why `dir_in` instead of simply `dir`?
Just because 1 means IN and 0 means OUT. But dir is fine since we are using the USBIP_DIR_xxx values
